ancestry_warning: FRANK architecture, ClayCode, ClayGraph and UnifiedDB share project ancestry; agreement among them is not independent replication.

items.assumption: ClayCode must represent FRANK recurrent loop dynamics, including halt/continuation and regime classification.
items.independent_check: Executable grammar/control probe independent of FRANK implementation details found the admitted G9 source itself needs relational comparisons and an explicit control form to express constructs it already uses.
items.counterhypothesis: Loop dynamics can remain external instrumentation and ClayCode need not represent control directly.
items.result: Counterhypothesis remains possible for some observability, but current G9 source already embeds control-like semantics; self-conformance requires at least surface completion.
items.scope: Minimal grammar/control completion only; no broad semantic redesign.

items.assumption: ClayCode needs a typed capability/effect boundary rather than ambient authority.
items.origin: FRANK safety history + current G9 CapabilityToken/EffectIntent design
items.independent_check: Current WASI authoritative documentation specifies a capability-based sandbox in which components begin without ambient authority and receive host-granted access explicitly.
items.counterhypothesis: Ordinary unrestricted host FFI plus application policy is simpler and sufficient.
items.result: Rejected as release default for ClayCode because it would erase the language/runtime authority boundary required by current acceptance and historical destructive-bypass regression constraints.

items.assumption: ClayCode should use explicit typed resource/ABI contracts for host interop.
items.independent_check: WebAssembly Component Model/WIT independently separates typed interface contracts and resources from implementation; the Canonical ABI defines cross-language representation.
items.counterhypothesis: Serialize arbitrary host calls through untyped JSON or shell text.
items.result: Untyped wire escape remains useful only behind Needle/adapter boundaries, not as the canonical ClayCode FFI contract.

items.assumption: Async/concurrency requires immediate new ClayCode semantic machinery.
items.independent_check: WASI 0.3 now provides native async func, stream<T> and future<T> in the Component Model/Canonical ABI, so a first implementation can lower typed ClayCode async/resource concepts into a host ABI instead of inventing a large scheduler semantics immediately.
items.counterhypothesis: ClayCode must own a complete bespoke scheduler before any real app can run.
items.result: Not supported for BASE sequencing; first prove typed lowering and observable cancellation/error semantics.

items.assumption: WASM/WASI should be the first ClayCode backend on Ubuntu.
items.independent_check: WASI 0.3/Wasmtime provide capabilities, typed components, HTTP/system APIs and native async, while MLIR provides a strong progressive-lowering model. This makes WASI high-value, but no target-host benchmark was run in this session.
items.counterhypothesis: Direct native/LLVM lowering reaches the Ubuntu-only v0.1 goal faster with lower runtime overhead.
items.next_test: Compile the same small ClayCode CLI/HTTP/effect exemplar to a native path and a WASI 0.3 component on Andreas' Ubuntu host; compare implementation effort, cold start, steady latency, binary size, capability isolation and diagnostics.

promotion_decision: NO_SCIENTIFIC_PROMOTION; executable counterexample authorizes a candidate grammar repair and implementation work only.
